classification.difficultyReason: Derives geometric formulae, differentiates connected quantities and converts length units before substitution.

content.prompt: In an equilateral triangle of side length $s$:

spec.description: Equilateral triangle with an altitude bisecting its horizontal base, two sloping side labels, two half-base labels and a right-angle marker.
spec.mathematics: Each sloping side is s, each half-base is s/2, and the altitude is h.
spec.answerVisibility: All labels and geometry are permanent question givens.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Show that the area is $A=\frac14s^2\sqrt3$ and the height is $h=\frac12s\sqrt3$.

answer.worked:
The altitude bisects the base and forms two right-angled triangles. By Pythagoras,
$$\begin{aligned}h^2&=s^2-\left(\frac{s}{2}\right)^2\\h^2&=\frac34s^2\\h&=\frac{\sqrt3}{2}s.\end{aligned}$$
Hence
$$\begin{aligned}A&=\frac12sh\\A&=\frac12s\left(\frac{\sqrt3}{2}s\right)\\A&=\frac{\sqrt3}{4}s^2.\end{aligned}$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: Find formulae for the rates of change of area and height in terms of the rate of change of side length.

children.label: c
children.prompt: Hence find the rate at which the area and the height are increasing when the side length is $12\text{ cm}$ and is increasing at $3\text{ mm/s}$.

answer.worked:
Use $s=12\text{ cm}=120\text{ mm}$ and $\frac{ds}{dt}=3\text{ mm/s}$.
$$\begin{aligned}\frac{dA}{dt}&=\frac12(120)\sqrt3(3)\\\frac{dA}{dt}&=180\sqrt3\text{ mm}^2/\text{s}.\end{aligned}$$
$$\begin{aligned}\frac{dh}{dt}&=\frac12\sqrt3(3)\\\frac{dh}{dt}&=\frac{3\sqrt3}{2}\text{ mm/s}.\end{aligned}$$
